title: Taco with meat and beans, no cheese

content.title: About
content.content: A taco is a traditional Mexican dish consisting of a soft or crispy tortilla filled with meat, beans, and various seasonings. This version uses lean beef, cooked red beans, fresh vegetables, and spices, without any cheese.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tacos originated in Mexico in the early 19th century as street food for laborers.
Traditionally the meat is grilled over an open flame, giving it a smoky flavor.
Beans in tacos provide a great source of plant protein and fiber.
Leaving out cheese makes the dish lighter and suitable for people with lactose intolerance.
Classic tacos are often served with lime, cilantro, and salsa.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beef and beans together supply a complete set of amino acids, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat is a good source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Fiber from beans
items.content: Beans are high in soluble and insoluble fiber, promoting digestive health.

items.title: Low in lactose
items.content: The absence of cheese makes the dish safe for those with lactose intolerance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and beans provide B12, niacin, and riboflavin, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Using fatty cuts of beef can increase saturated fat levels, which may be a concern for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt and sauces can raise sodium intake, which should be limited for hypertension.

items.title: Bean allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to beans and should avoid this ingredient.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of meat, beans, and tortilla makes the dish relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Warm the tortilla, then fill it with beef, beans, fresh veggies (tomatoes, onion, lettuce) and seasonings. Optional toppings include salsa, guacamole, or a squeeze of lime.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared tacos are best eaten immediately. If needed, store meat and beans separately in airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Tortillas can be kept at room temperature in a sealed bag for up to 5 days.
